modules.title: Recursion Fundamentals
modules.summary: Core mental models for recursive problem solving, correctness, and performance.
modules.detailedContent: This module builds a deep foundation for recursion by focusing on call-stack behavior, subproblem design, and invariant-based reasoning. Learners explore how to define strict base cases, prove termination using decreasing measures, and trace stack frames for both pre-order and post-order computation. The content also covers common implementation pitfalls such as hidden shared state, incorrect return propagation, and missing branch coverage. By the end, learners should be able to convert verbal problem statements into recursive formulations with explicit correctness arguments and complexity estimates.
learningOutcomes: Define base cases that are complete and non-overlapping.
Trace recursive execution using stack snapshots and return values.
Reason about termination with strictly decreasing progress measures.
Estimate time and space complexity for linear and branching recursion.

modules.title: Recursion Tracing and Debugging
modules.summary: Practical debugging workflows for recursive code and stack-level diagnostics.
modules.detailedContent: This module focuses on professional debugging workflows for recursive functions. Learners practice instrumenting recursion with structured logs, indentation-based call-depth markers, and deterministic replay of execution paths. The module discusses crash signatures for runaway recursion, stack overflows, and wrong-branch exits. It also introduces assertion-driven debugging, memo inspection, and tracing of mutation across frames. Through repeated trace exercises, learners improve their ability to isolate the exact call where invariants break and produce targeted fixes with regression tests.
learningOutcomes: Build reproducible traces of recursive execution paths.
Identify failure frames from stack overflow and assertion logs.
Use call-depth instrumentation to diagnose branch divergence.
Write regression tests that lock down fixed recursive bugs.

modules.title: Recursion on Trees and Graphs
modules.summary: Applying recursion to hierarchical and connected data structures.
modules.detailedContent: This module extends recursion into structural algorithms on trees and graph-like structures. Learners study traversal patterns, divide-and-conquer aggregation, and safe handling of branching factor growth. For trees, the module covers recursive DFS variants, height/diameter style aggregations, and subtree summarization. For graph scenarios, it introduces visited-state guarding to prevent cycles and repeated work. Special emphasis is given to designing return contracts that combine local node information with child results in a composable way.
learningOutcomes: Implement recursive DFS for tree traversals and subtree metrics.
Design return contracts for multi-child aggregation problems.
Prevent cycles with visited-state checks in recursive graph walks.
Analyze recursion depth and branching impact on complexity.

modules.title: Dynamic Programming via Recursion
modules.summary: Transforming expensive recursion into efficient memoized and tabulated solutions.
modules.detailedContent: This module links recursion to dynamic programming through overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure analysis. Learners start from naive recursive solutions, derive recurrence equations, and then apply memoization to eliminate duplicate work. The module compares top-down memo recursion with bottom-up tabulation, including trade-offs in readability, stack usage, and iterative state ordering. It also covers cache-key design, invalid-state handling, and correctness checks for transitions. By completion, learners should confidently refactor exponential recursion into polynomial-time approaches.
learningOutcomes: Detect overlapping subproblems in naive recursion.
Add memo caches with valid key and value semantics.
Compare top-down and bottom-up strategies for the same recurrence.
Validate transition rules and edge-state initialization.

modules.title: Backtracking with Recursion
modules.summary: Systematic search with recursive branching, constraints, and pruning.
modules.detailedContent: This module teaches backtracking as a disciplined recursive search strategy. Learners build candidate states incrementally, validate constraints early, and prune branches that cannot produce valid solutions. The curriculum covers include/exclude recursion patterns, permutation/combination generation, and state rollback mechanics. It also highlights performance engineering through ordering heuristics, forward checking, and bounding functions. Learners finish with the ability to construct clean, testable backtracking templates for scheduling, puzzle solving, and constrained combinatorics.
learningOutcomes: Model backtracking state with explicit choose-explore-unchoose flow.
Apply constraint checks early to reduce branching.
Design pruning rules that are safe and high impact.
Implement permutation and combination generators with rollback.
